title: Microglia mediate motor memory decay through activity-dependent phagocytosis of myelin sheaths
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02505-8Hu et al. showed that motor memory decay involves microglia engulfing memory-related myelin sheaths. Reduced engram activity lowers CD47, a ‘don’t eat me’ signal, thus promoting microglia-mediated myelin clearance and facilitating memory decay.

title: Distinct prelimbic microcircuits control sensory and affective dimensions of neuropathic pain
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02498-4Gan et al. report the cellular mechanisms underlying dysbalance of prefrontal brain activity in mice with neuropathic pain and delineate the circuitry through which the prefrontal cortex exerts top-down control of sensory and emotional aspects of pain.

title: Enhancer-targeted CRISPR-A rescues haploinsufficiency and mutant phenotypes in organoid models of autism
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02504-9CRISPR activation targeted to enhancers of autism risk genes CHD8 and SCN2A selectively increased expression and reversed mutant phenotypes in both patient-derived and gene-edited neuron and cortical organoid models of autism.

title: Losing a Single “Molecular Brake” Gene Triggers Brain Overgrowth
summary: What happens when developing brain stem cells lose a key genetic brake? Using single-cell lineage tracing, researchers found missing Pten drives stem cells to produce 25% more neurons and excess enlarged astrocytes, rerouting signaling through the MAPK pathway.

title: Intolerance of Uncertainty Surged 3x Faster Since 2012
summary: Is rising youth anxiety just increased mental health awareness—or a real surge in psychological distress? Analyzing over 35,000 college students from 1992 to 2023, researchers found that intolerance of uncertainty rose three times faster after 2012.

title: Ultraprocessed Foods Alter Food-Reward Brain Activity
summary: Even when calories, sugar, and fat are identical, industrial food processing changes how the young brain responds to food. A new study reveals that two weeks on an ultraprocessed diet blunts orbitofrontal cortex reward activity in adults ages 18 to 21.

title: Brain Computes Motion Direction Independently From the Eye
summary: How does your brain instantly know which way a fast-moving object is heading? Using a new mapping tool across 46,000 brain cells, scientists discovered in Nature that the brain doesn't just take the eye's word for motion direction, specialized midbrain neurons compute it on their own.

title: Sour Tastes Hijack the Tongue to Mute Sweetness, Bitterness, and Saltiness
summary: Why does a sour bite overpower sweet, salty, and bitter flavors? A new study reveals that taste buds act as miniature processing hubs, releasing serotonin in response to sourness to mute competing flavors before signals ever reach the brain.

title: Older Brains Lose Synchronization Between Movement and Body Temperature
summary: Even when 24-hour circadian rhythms persist into old age, faster multi-hour "ultradian" rhythms weaken significantly. New research shows aging decouples physical activity from core body temperature while triggering immune gene activation and neuronal loss inside the brain's master clock.

title: Scent and Memory: Why Novelty Boosts Recall in Older Adults
summary: Can diffusing lavender really sharpen your memory? A new study reveals that scent alone doesn't boost recall, unless older adults experience it as a novel sensory cue at the very beginning of learning.

title: How ADHD Shapes Breathing and Time Perception
summary: ADHD reaches far beyond inattention and hyperactivity. New studies reveal that the condition alters breathing patterns, triggers chronic time pressure, lowers regional brain iron in youth, and influences problem drinking in young adults.

title: How Lead Exposure Erodes Long-Term Memory

title: Why Viruses Make You Sneeze: COVID Proteins Directly Hijack Sensory Nerves
summary: Why do colds, flu, and COVID make us sneeze, cough, and ache? Researchers found the SARS-CoV-2 enzymes directly hijack pain-sensing airway nerves via the "wasabi receptor" (TRPA1), triggering symptoms independently of immune inflammation.

title: Genetic Switch Helped Evolve the Large Primate Brain
summary: How did the human brain evolve to be so large and complex? Researchers discovered a primate-specific DNA regulatory switch controlling the shared DACH1 gene, boosting specialized basal radial glia stem cells that build the cerebral cortex without needing new genes.

title: CRISPR Enhancer Editing Rescues Autism Brain Organoids
summary: Rather than cutting DNA, scientists used precision CRISPR activation aimed at natural gene "dials" to boost healthy copies of CHD8 and SCN2A in human brain organoids, restoring normal tissue growth and neuronal firing exclusively in mutated cells.
